text:
maria: Heads-up — found a deterministic repro where x-request-id gets dropped after our SDK retry in the Node sampleapp. Repro steps below, attaching logs. Anyone else seen this?

sam: I remember a similar note from Python a while back, but behavior was different. Curious if this is OTEL hook ordering or our retry wrapper.

eli: Can you paste the minimal snippet + logs? quick guesses: fetch cloning behavior, or context loss across async retry.

maria: repro (super small):

```js
// sampleapp: outbound-wrapper.js
async function callWithRetry(url, headers) {
  let attempts = 0;
  while (attempts < 3) {
    attempts++
    // we expect x-request-id to be present here (injected by otel hook)
    const res = await fetch(url, { headers });
    if (res.ok) return res;
  }
  throw new Error('failed');
}

// elsewhere, otel hook does: span.setAttribute('request_id', reqId); // and relies on instrumentation to inject header
```

Logs show first attempt includes `x-request-id: abc123` but second attempt has no header. stack traces show retry wrapper reusing the same headers object but header missing at the time of the second fetch.

jess: hmm. Do we instrument fetch or the higher-level SDK request function? If OTEL hook is on the outgoing span and instrumentation injects headers at span start, a retry that starts a new span might not have the previous request_id.

noelle: quick diagnostic: does the retry wrapper run in a different async context so the OTEL context token isn't available on retry? Node async hooks + some promise libraries can break context propagation.

telemetry-bot: trace lookup: trace_id=00f1a... span=outbound.http start=1767801234. First attempt: attribute.request_id=abc123. Second attempt: attribute.request_id=null.

sam: For parity notes: Python requests-based retry preserved header in our sampleapp because we explicitly carry headers in the retry wrapper. Node relies on instrumentation to inject per-span, so if span isnt propagated we lose it. So this is a SDK parity + hook-order issue.

eli: Proposed short-term fix: mutate headers object in the retry wrapper to ensure x-request-id is copied from current context before each attempt. Long-term: ensure our OTEL hook attaches header earlier (instrument the fetch adapter) or ensure context propagation across retries.

maria: I verified quick workaround: before each fetch attempt do: `headers['x-request-id'] ||= currentReqIdFromContext()` — works in repro. But this is a bandaid, we should patch the SDK so sampleapps have consistent behavior.

jess: can we add a unit/e2e to the sampleapp telemetry harness that does 2 failing attempts then succeeds and asserts header present on every outbound? If so we can prevent regressions.

eli: yes. I'll open a PR with: 1) fix in node sdk retry wrapper to preserve/inject request-id, 2) add e2e in sampleapp, 3) add note in SDK parity doc. Assigning to myself.

noelle: also flag this in onboarding docs — mention that rapid retries can surface otel context propagation issues on older Node versions (12/14).

sam: and add a small paragraph in the telemetry README: recommended pattern is to explicitly copy critical headers in retry wrappers, or use our instrumented fetch client.

maria: thanks — can you include a small code comment in PR explaining why we do the explicit header copy (context loss + fetch clone caveat)? saves future confusion. :thumbsup:

eli: will do. PR will reference this thread and include a minimal repro test and a changelog entry.

jess: please add label `devex-telemetry` + `sdk-parity` and ping @eng-platform for a quick review.

maria: i'll update the sampleapp onboarding note so new users hitting this don't think it's a bug in their infra. thanks all.

telemetry-bot: Note: added trace link to issue #4521 for triage.

sam: awesome. followup: create a small checklist for release (docs, test, changelog, rollout).

maria: copying checklist into the PR description when it's up.

eli: PR opened: https://git.redwood/infer/pull/789 (wip)

jess: will review later today. :rocket:
